'''''Gamochaeta antillana''''', the '''delicate everlasting''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to the [[Greater Antilles]] and to the southeastern United States (from [[Florida]] to [[Louisiana]]). It has also become naturalized in other places (South America, Europe, Australia, [[New Zealand]], [[Texas]], [[California]], the [[Carolinas]], etc.).<ref name=gln>[http://www.guynesom.com/Gamochaetarecords.pdf Guy L. Nesom 2004. New distribution records for ''Gamochaeta'' (Asteraceae: Gnaphalieae) in the United States. Sida 21(2): 1175–1185.]</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Gamochaeta%20antillana.png|title=Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map|website=bonap.net}}</ref><ref>Zuloaga, F. O., O. Morrone, M. J. Belgrano, C. Marticorena & E. Marchesi. (eds.) 2008. Catálogo de las plantas vasculares del Cono Sur. Monographs in Systematic Botany from the Missouri Botanical Garden 107(1–3): i–xcvi, 1–3348.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:655146#|title=Gamochaeta antillana  – Atlas of Living Australia|first=Atlas of Living|last=Australia|website=bie.ala.org.au}}</ref>

''Gamochaeta antillana'' is an annual herb up to {{convert|40|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall, producing a taproot. Leaves are up to {{convert|4|cm|in|abbr=on}} long. The plant forms many small flower heads in elongated arrays and also in tightly packed clumps. Each head contains 3–5 purple disc flowers but no ray flowers.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250066791 Flora of North America, ''Gamochaeta antillana'' (Urban) Anderberg, 1991. Delicate everlasting ]</ref>

''Gamochaeta antillana'' is similar to ''[[Gamochaeta falcata|G. falcata]],'' and many ''Gamochaeta antillana'' specimens from the eastern United States have long been misidentified as ''[[Gamochaeta falcata|G. falcata]].''<ref name=gln/>
